Key observations:
- **Green, moist stems** while pods are brown and fully matured/dried
- Surrounding plant material is brown and dead
- Pods appear normal (just dried/mature), no lesions
- Classic contrast: green living stem vs. dried brown pods

This strongly suggests **Green_stem_disorder**. Let me verify with reference images.
The Green_stem_disorder reference is an excellent match — top-right panel shows the identical scenario (green stem, brown mature pods, dark soil). Let me view the remaining required references.

All evidence confirms the diagnosis. The test image shows:
- **Green, moist stems** contrasting with fully dried/brown mature pods
- Dark soil background, late-season field setting
- No lesions, spots, mold, or other pathological markers on any tissue
- Neighboring plant material all brown and dead — this plant's stem alone remains green

The Green_stem_disorder reference collage (top-right panel) is nearly identical to the test image — same green stem, same brown dry pods, same dark soil.

No other class fits: no leaf lesions (rules out Septoria, Cercospora, Frogeye, etc.), no stem cankers or rot (rules out Brown Stem Rot, Phytophthora, Charcoal Rot), no white mold or pycnidia, no root symptoms visible.
